header: Test vectors for HPKE (RFC 9180) single-shot Open in base mode
using the ML-KEM-1024 KEM from draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05. The recipient
private key skRm is the 64-byte d || z seed. Valid cases include
ikmE, the 32-byte encapsulation randomness, so deterministic
encapsulation reproduces enc and ct; the exceptions are the
ImplicitRejection, Strcmp, and MalleableCiphertext cases, whose ct is
sealed under the ML-KEM implicit-rejection secret, which no
encapsulation produces. Given (skRm, info, aad, enc, ct) an
implementation runs SetupBaseR then Open and must recover pt for
valid cases or reject invalid cases. Acceptable cases are
interoperability probes that an RFC-literal implementation opens; an
implementation may reject them, but if it opens one it must recover

AppendedByteCiphertext.description: A trailing byte was appended to the AEAD ciphertext.

EmbeddedZeroAad.description: The AEAD associated data contains embedded zero bytes.

EmbeddedZeroInfo.description: The HPKE info contains embedded zero bytes, catching a consumer that mishandles them (e.g. treats info as null-terminated).

EmbeddedZeroPlaintext.description: The plaintext contains embedded zero bytes.

EmptyAad.description: The AEAD associated data is empty.

EmptyCiphertext.description: The AEAD ciphertext is empty (shorter than one tag).

EmptyInfo.description: The HPKE info string is empty.

EmptyPlaintext.description: The sealed plaintext is empty, so ct is the Nt-byte AEAD tag alone; Open must succeed and return an empty plaintext. hpke-rs-rust-crypto 0.4.0 through 0.6.0 rejected every ciphertext of at most Nt bytes on Open (its AEAD checked msg.len() <= tag_length instead of <); fixed in 0.6.1.
EmptyPlaintext.effect: Interoperability failure: the receiver cannot open messages with an empty plaintext, such as ones that only authenticate aad.

ImplicitRejection.description: enc has the correct length but fails the re-encryption check of ML-KEM.Decaps (a valid enc with one bit flipped, or all zeros). FIPS 203 Algorithm 18 does not fail here: it implicitly rejects and returns K-bar = J(z || c), where z is the second half of skRm. draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 Section 3 defines HPKE Decap as ML-KEM.Decaps, with DecapError only for the FIPS 203 input checks. ct is sealed under K-bar, so Open must succeed. An implementation that returns an error on implicit rejection, or computes K-bar incorrectly, fails.

LongInfo.description: info is 1024 bytes, above the RECOMMENDED 64-byte limit of RFC 9180 Section 7.2.1 but far below the maximum (2^61 - 91 bytes for HKDF-SHA256, 2^125 - 155 for HKDF-SHA384 and HKDF-SHA512). An implementation may reject it because of an input length limit; if it accepts it, it must recover pt.

LongPlaintext.description: A 512-byte plaintext, exercising the AEAD across multiple blocks.

MalleableCiphertext.description: skRm and enc are the seed and ciphertext of a MalleableCiphertext case in mlkem_*_test.json: a valid ciphertext modified at one byte position of c1 or c2. A correct ML-KEM.Decaps implicitly rejects and returns K-bar = J(z || c), the expected K of the upstream case. ct is sealed under K-bar, so Open must succeed. A re-encryption comparison that skips this byte position returns a different shared secret, and Open fails.

MismatchedEncCt.description: enc and ct come from two different encapsulations to the same recipient, so the AEAD key derived from enc does not match the one that sealed ct; Open must fail.

ModifiedCiphertext.description: A bit of the AEAD ciphertext body was flipped.

ModifiedEnc.description: enc is a valid encapsulation with the low bit of its first byte (a c1 coefficient) flipped, and ct is sealed under the original shared secret. The change is lost in decompression, so K-PKE.Decrypt still returns the original message m and only the re-encryption comparison in ML-KEM.Decaps (FIPS 203 Algorithm 18) detects it. A correct Decaps implicitly rejects, returning K-bar = J(z || c), and Open fails. A Decaps that skips the comparison returns the original shared secret, and Open succeeds.

ModifiedTag.description: The AEAD authentication tag was modified: a bit of its first or last byte was flipped, or the whole tag was replaced by zero bytes.

Pseudorandom.description: A valid HPKE base-mode ciphertext with deterministic encapsulation from ikmE, the randomness m passed to FIPS 203 ML-KEM.Encaps_internal (draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 Appendix A).

RecommendedLimitInfo.description: info is 64 bytes, the RECOMMENDED limit for info in RFC 9180 Section 7.2.1, chosen there to "enable interoperability with implementations that statically allocate memory for these inputs". Open must succeed.

SeedAllOnes.description: The recipient private key is the all-one (0xFF) 64-byte seed; key derivation must succeed and be deterministic.

SeedAllZero.description: The recipient private key is the all-zero 64-byte seed. Every 64-byte string is a valid ML-KEM d || z seed (FIPS 203), so key derivation must succeed and be deterministic.

Strcmp.description: skRm and enc are the seed and ciphertext of the Strcmp case in mlkem_*_test.json. If ML-KEM.Decaps compares c with its re-encryption using strcmp(), a zero byte ends the comparison early and the ciphertext is wrongly accepted. A correct Decaps implicitly rejects and returns K-bar = J(z || c), the expected K of the upstream case. ct is sealed under K-bar, so Open must succeed.

TagOnlyCiphertext.description: ct is exactly Nt = 16 bytes, the length of an empty-plaintext ciphertext, but is not the empty-plaintext ciphertext for this key, nonce, and aad (it is the tag of the base message with the body removed). Open must fail rather than return an empty plaintext.

TrailingZeroAad.description: aad is the sealed aad followed by one zero byte. A receiver that treats aad as a null-terminated string or strips trailing zero bytes accepts; Open must fail.

TrailingZeroInfo.description: info is the sealed info followed by one zero byte. A receiver that treats info as a null-terminated string or strips trailing zero bytes derives the sender's key and accepts; info is an arbitrary byte string bound into the key schedule (RFC 9180 Section 5.1), so Open must fail.

TruncatedCiphertext.description: The AEAD ciphertext is truncated below the tag length.

WrongAad.description: The aad differs from the one sealed under; accepting it would bypass AEAD authentication of the associated data.

WrongInfo.description: The info differs from the one sealed under, so the key schedule derives a different key; accepting it would bypass the info binding (RFC 9180 Section 5.1).

WrongLengthEnc.description: enc does not have the KEM's Nenc length (empty, short, long, or the length of a different ML-KEM parameter set) and must be rejected by SetupBaseR.

WrongRecipientEnc.description: enc and ct are a valid encapsulation and sealing for a different recipient key. Decapsulating under this skRm yields a different shared secret, so Open must fail.
